why: The student links the bound to each row's own length. They see that a[0].length is enough only for a square board, and that a general 2-D array needs a[i].length because its rows can have different lengths (a ragged array). This relational point comes from how Java 2-D arrays work, but the student writes no full method.

concepts.quote: For a 3 × 3 board I would use a[0].length, but for any 2-D array I need a[i].length.
concepts.why: Each row is its own array, so rows can differ in length (ragged). The column bound must therefore be read from each row.

concepts.quote: for any 2-D array I need a[i].length
concepts.why: The student uses the length field so the loop bound follows the real size of each row, not a fixed width.
Treating a[i] as row i, a 1-D array with its own length, shows the student knows the first index picks the row.
The answer says nothing about arrays with three or more dimensions.
